```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(p8105.datasets)
data("weather_df")
library(patchwork)

weather_df
```

```{r}
weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax, color = name)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5)
```

##Labels
```{r}
weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax, color = name)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Temperature plot",
    x = "Minimum daily temperature (C)",
    y = "Maximum daily temperature (C)",
    caption = "Data from rnoa package; temperature in 2017"
  )
```


## Scales
  gives you a way to have control
Start with same plot
```{r}
weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax, color = name)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Temperature plot",
    x = "Minimum daily temperature (C)",
    y = "Maximum daily temperature (C)",
    caption = "Data from rnoa package; temperature in 2017"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(-15, 0, 15),
    labels = c("-15C", "0", "15")
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous (
    position = "right"
  )
#don't want original spacing, scale_x allows you to change it
#scal_y lets you do a transformation of data: eg "sqrt", "log", or "right
```

```{r}
weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax, color = name)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Temperature plot",
    x = "Minimum daily temperature (C)",
    y = "Maximum daily temperature (C)",
    caption = "Data from rnoa package; temperature in 2017") +
  scale_color_hue(
    name = "location") +
  viridis:: scale_color_viridis(
    name = "Location",
    discrete = TRUE
  )



#Defined mapping between the color variable and the name  
  #scale_color can edit color feature, can adjust hue
#scale_x - change title of caption
  #in scale if we want to change color of the name, can change caption to location (what all the locations are called)
#viridis package - scale color viridis assumes it is a continuous variable, have to specify discrete
  #viridis pallet: if you show this to someone who is color blind, it will be more accessible to them.

```


#Themes
Where this lies on my plot doesn't depend on difference between variable and color, just absent of data
Grey background and white lines dont depend on data, just has to do with overall plot structure and appearance
or theme

Shift the legend:
```{r}
weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax, color = name)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Temperature plot",
    x = "Minimum daily temperature (C)",
    y = "Maximum daily temperature (C)",
    caption = "Data from rnoa package; temperature in 2017") +
  scale_color_hue(
    name = "location") +
  viridis:: scale_color_viridis(
    name = "Location",
    discrete = TRUE
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```


Change the overall theme - on default ggplot uses grey and white 
  -in changing theme wipes the slate and makes it brand new, if want to do theme minimal have to do the theme first
```{r}


weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax, color = name)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Temperature plot",
    x = "Minimum daily temperature (C)",
    y = "Maximum daily temperature (C)",
    caption = "Data from rnoa package; temperature in 2017") +
  scale_color_hue(
    name = "location") +
  viridis:: scale_color_viridis(
    name = "Location",
    discrete = TRUE
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```


## Setting options
determine theme for every plot in document
ggplot2.continuous. fill = "viridis" - will fill color for points later on
all options ensure viridis color pallet and legend on bottom
out.width shrinks it down a little bit: use this in the future of all markdowns to ensure that it will be there
```{r}
library(tidyverse)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  fig.width = 6,
  fig.asp = 0.6,
  out.width = "90%"
)

theme_set(theme_minimal() + theme(legend,position = "bottom"))

options(
  ggplot2.continuous.colour = "viridis",
  ggplot2.continuous.fill = "viridis"
)

scale_colour_discrete = scale_color_viridis_d
scale_colour_continuous = scale_color_viridis_d
```


## Data args in 'geom'

```{r}
central_park = weather_df |> 
  filter(name == "CentralPark_NY")

waikiki = weather_df |> 
  filter(name == "Molokai_HI")

ggplot(data = waikiki, aes(x = date, y = tmax, color = name)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line(data =central_park)
```
Use mostly for summary that is more complicated. Will create a separate dataset for each argument

## 'Patchwork'
remember faceting? Creating the exact same plot. Create plot separately for each name
putting a scatterplot next to a scatterplot is not possible with facceting

```{r}
weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, fill = name)) +
  geom_density ( alpha = 0.5) +
  facet_grid(. ~ name)
```



```{r}
tmax_tmin_p = 
  weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y= tmax, color = name)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
tmax_tmin_p

prcp_dens_p = 
  weather_df |> 
  filter(prcp > 0) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = prcp, fill = name)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5)
prcp_dens_p

tmax_date = 
  weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = date, y = tmax, color = name)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
tmax_date

(tmax_tmin_p + prcp_dens_p) / tmax_date
```
create individual panels and use patchwork to join them
